sentences.text:
-----
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi
-----
For the Petitioner : Mr. S.S. Choudhary, Advocate

For the State : Mr. Shree Prakash Jha, A.P.P.
 -----
02/14.05.2024 Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for  the State.

2. The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in connection with Complaint Case No.28/2023,
registered for the alleged offence under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, pending in the Court of the learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Rajmahal.

entities.text: Court of the learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Rajmahal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is the husband of the complainant and there are general and omnibus allegations against the petitioner as well as in-laws and in-laws have been provided privilege of anticipatory bail by the learned Sessions Judge.
4. Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer.

5. Looking into solemn affirmation, it transpires that there are general and omnibus allegations against the petitioner, who happened to be the husband and mode of torture is not disclosed in the complaint.
6.
In the attending facts and circumstances of the case, I am inclined to extend the privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
Accordingly, the above-named petitioner is directed to surrender before the learned Court within three weeks from today and in the event of his arrest or surrender

,
he will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate,
Rajmahal in connection with Complaint Case No.28/2023, subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
